title: No fertility refund: speculative-decoding acceptance across 21 languages (data and code)
description:
Per-item speculative-decoding acceptance for two built-in self-drafters, Qwen3.5-9B with its MTP head and Gemma 4 E4B with its assistant, on 200 FLORES-200 devtest sentences in each of 21 languages, with the code that measures it exactly for greedy lossless speculation (K = 1..5).

Result: no fertility refund. Under decision rules stated by the author before the runs (not independently verifiable; one gate amendment followed the first run), every gate passed and both kill rules fired in both families on their point estimates. Acceptance does not rise with fertility: the partial Spearman ρ of AL at K=3 with the token ratio, controlling for competence, is −0.656 for Gemma and −0.033 for Qwen (language-bootstrap interval −0.53 to 0.52; Qwen's F2′ median 0.172 has language-bootstrap interval 0.152 to 0.224, across its 0.20 threshold). Every other language has lower acceptance length than English, so the refund fraction is negative wherever it is defined. Qwen's half of the verdict rests on point estimates.

Why (exploratory). Other languages have more continuation tokens than English, which are easier to draft (+0.026 / +0.055 step-1 acceptance), but the within-tag component of the gap to English is negative (−0.195 / −0.426), in all 20 languages; word-start, continuation and other tokens are each accepted less often than in English in every language.

Serving follow-up (descriptive, no decision rules). The same drafters, plus two EAGLE-3 heads for Qwen3-8B, in vLLM 0.31.0 on one A100. At batch 1 and K = 3, for both built-in drafters, every non-English language of six gets a smaller wall-clock speedup than English: Qwen 1.41–1.73 against 1.94, Gemma 1.23–1.86 against 2.38. Under sampling (T = 0, 0.7, 1.0) the Spearman ρ of AL with the token ratio stays negative for both (−0.21 to −0.68). A multilingual EAGLE-3 head shows ρ ≈ 0 over all 21 languages and is weak in English (AL 1.70 against 2.42 for the general head); its target produces many degenerate sampled outputs in a few languages, and without the languages above 10% invalid items its ρ is +0.42 at T = 0 (16 languages; post hoc), but only +0.08 to +0.42 across exclusion thresholds of 5–50%, so at most weakly positive. One serving run. In vLLM, speculative greedy output often differs from plain greedy output (only half of Qwen's Amharic outputs at K = 1 are identical), so the speedups are latency ratios over the same inputs, not at identical output.

Version 1.4 corrects the paper: definitions, the token-ratio description, the Qwen caveat, missing citations and the figures. Data, code and results are unchanged.

Version 1.3 adds the paper (paper/fert-refund-paper.pdf), which carries its own AI-use statement. Data, code and results are unchanged.

Version 1.2 adds an exclusion-threshold sweep to the sensitivity check: the multilingual head's positive trend reported in v1.1 (+0.42) is the largest across thresholds of 5–50%, so it is at most weakly positive and its sign depends on the threshold.

Version 1.1 corrects v1.0's description of the multilingual EAGLE-3 head as flat in fertility, which held only with degenerate outputs included, and adds post-hoc analyses (an invalid-item sensitivity check, the six-language latency correlation, and calibration identity with the probe). Data and the code that produced them are unchanged.

Not claimed: an externally verifiable preregistration; recorded provenance for run 2: it predates recorded model revisions and code fingerprints, the verdict code exempts its files by identity, and the shipped runner and verdict code are later versions (the emulation library is unchanged); decision rules for the serving follow-up. See README.md.

FLORES-200 references: NLLB Team et al. (2022), arXiv:2207.04672, CC BY-SA 4.0. Licence: CC BY-SA 4.0; the code (code/, reproduce.sh) is additionally offered under the MIT License (LICENSE-CODE).
